Published in [Gaoxy v0.11.1](https://github.com/gsmlg-dev/gaoxy/releases/tag/v0.11.1), with all six coordinated Hex packages available at 0.11.1.

HTTP/1 polling now keeps an exactly full `max_buffer_bytes` buffer valid. One admitted observation can report pending input or peer closure; only an actual excess byte returns `:buffer_limit`, without extending the retained pipeline. That error consumes the observation byte and is terminal: retain the returned `Plug.Conn` and abort it. No application observation margin or private socket state is required.

Validation: independent review; all 10 exact-source prerequisite jobs; the full 361-case ordinary gate; H1/H2/H3 browser and standalone checks; byte/checksum verification of all six public Hex archives and eight GitHub assets. A fresh Hex-only install passed all six public TCP regressions for delayed/coalesced input, inclusive keep-alive reuse, bounded excess rejection and full-buffer peer closure. Fresh general public consumers passed seven additional cases.

Release source/tag: `09715de3f165db134e287e1ea5fd4e93b1325905`.
[Acceptance and evidence](https://github.com/gsmlg-dev/gaoxy/blob/main/docs/acceptance/release-0.11.1.md).
